name: Long Forms
description: An album about music that unfolds over many bars instead of looping one: a rondo built with form and seeded variants, a thirty-two bar arc shaped by one envelope, a subject developed by inversion, retrograde and sequence, a round and a mensuration canon, pianos that phase apart, figures that grow and shrink, tempo canons that converge, melodies grown from integer sequences, sieves and rewriting systems, a twelve-tone row, change ringing and a finale that plays once and stops. Every sketch names the technique it uses in its comments.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Rondo in Form
sketches.description: A rondo laid out with form: the refrain returns between two episodes, each time as a seeded variant (A, A', A''), so its ornaments change while its tune stays. Each section starts its part from the beginning.

sketches.name: Thirty-Two Bar Arc
sketches.description: One breakpoint envelope shapes brightness and loudness over thirty-two bars, while parts enter, leave, fade in, fade out and change for a window of bars. Listen through once: after bar 32 only the pad remains, breathing on its own.

sketches.name: Mirror Subject
sketches.description: A two-bar subject developed in five sections: stated plainly, inverted, played backwards, sequenced one step higher each bar and broken into fragments, while the bass plays the subject four times slower.

sketches.name: Round Table
sketches.description: A round in three voices made by canon, each entering a bar later and an octave higher, over a cello that plays the same tune at half and quarter speed with prolation.

sketches.name: Drifting Pianos
sketches.description: Phasing after Steve Reich: two pianos play the same twelve-note figure, but phase shifts the second one a twelfth of a bar further each bar, so it walks through every alignment and lines up again after twelve bars.

sketches.name: Growing Figures
sketches.description: Additive and subtractive processes in the manner of Philip Glass: one eight-note figure grows by a note each bar in one voice and loses a note each bar in the other, so the two breathe against each other.
sketches.source:
setcpm(112/4)

const figure = n("0 2 4 5 7 5 4 2").scale("A:minor")

// additive cuts the figure into eight steps and plays one step more each bar, stretched to fill it
grow: figure.transpose(12).additive(8)
  .s("square").pw(.3).lpf(2400).decay(.12).sustain(0)
  .delay(.25).delaytime(3/16).pan(.35).gain(.15)

// subtractive plays one step fewer each bar
shrink: figure.subtractive(8)
  .s("triangle").timbre("bright").decay(.2).sustain(0).pan(.65).gain(.2)

// A steady floor under the process
pad: note("<[a3,c4,e4] [f3,a3,c4]>").slow(4).s("sawtooth").unison(3).detune(.2)
  .attack(1).release(2).lpf(1200).room(.6).gain(.12)
bass: note("<a1 f1>").slow(4).s("sine").attack(.3).sustain(.8).release(1).gain(.3)
kick: s("bd*4").lpf(250).gain(.45)

sketches.name: Converging Clocks
sketches.description: A tempo canon after Conlon Nancarrow: converge plays one figure at speeds 1, 9/8 and 5/4, shifted so all three reach the start of the figure together every eight bars, where a bell rings.

sketches.name: Infinity Series
sketches.description: Every part is a named integer sequence: Nørgård's self-similar infinity series for the melody, the ruler sequence for hat accents, Thue-Morse rims, van der Corput panning, Fibonacci bells modulo five and a bass counting Collatz steps.

sketches.name: Sieve Machine
sketches.description: Rhythms from number theory: sieves of residue classes after Xenakis, a Sturmian rhythm of five hits in thirteen, clicks on prime steps that thin out over time and a bass that reads the digits of the counting numbers in base five.

sketches.name: Rewriting Garden
sketches.description: Lindenmayer systems: a melody grown by rewriting degrees for six generations, a drum line rewritten from a single kick, and rims on the Fibonacci word.

sketches.name: Twelve Tones
sketches.description: A twelve-tone row and its forms: the upper voice walks through the prime, an inversion, a retrograde and a retrograde inversion, two bars each, while the lower voice plays slower forms of the same row.

sketches.name: Change Ringing
sketches.description: Six bells ring plain hunt, a new row every bar, returning to rounds after twelve bars, while a chime above walks through the orderings of four notes with permute.

sketches.name: Finale, Once
sketches.description: A twenty-bar finale that plays once and stops: a motif, its inversion climbing in sequence, then the motif again as a variant, over drums laid out by their own form with fills and a closing crash, and a pad that fades away at the end.
